Subject: ACME POC  proposed success criteria & integration plan

Hi Alex / Priya  great to meet you on today's discovery call. Thanks for walking through the ACME use case; below is my recap, proposed success criteria for the 2-week POC, and a high-level integration checklist. Please confirm or add anything I missed.

POC objective:
- Validate Redwood inference for in-app summarization + tool-calling for ticket triage.

Success criteria (pass/fail metrics):
1) Functional: 80% of sampled tickets are auto-classified correctly (per ACME taxonomy) vs. baseline manual labeling.
2) Latency: 95th percentile inference latency < 250ms for 512-token responses under test load.
3) Stability: No more than 2 errors per 1k requests (timeouts, 5xx) during test window.
4) Integration: Streaming responses and tool-calling endpoints work end-to-end in ACME staging.

Evaluation plan:
- Redwood will provide an eval prompt set (50 tickets) + streaming demo scripts.
- ACME will run a 48-hour soak in staging with representative traffic (we'll agree traffic profile).
- Post-test: joint review with sample scoring and qualitative feedback.

Timeline & ownership:
- Week 0 (this week): finalize success criteria & access (ACME to provide staging keys, sample tickets). Owner: Marissa (Redwood) / Alex (ACME)
- Week 1: Integration (SDK + API routes, streaming). Owner: Dylan (Redwood eng) / Priya (ACME eng)
- Week 2: Soak & evaluation, joint review. Owner: Monica (CS) / Alex (ACME)

Integration checklist (high-level):
- Provide Redwood SDK + sample code (Node/Python).
- API routes required: /v1/generate (streaming support), /v1/tool_call (webhook-style callbacks), embeddings endpoints for indexing.
- Auth: short-lived key for staging, IP allowlist for ACME testing.
- Logging & observability: token-level cost logs and latency traces (console link provided).

Attachments: redwood-poc-eval-plan.pdf, redwood-sdk-integration-guide.md, mutual action plan (spreadsheet).

Next steps requested:
1) Alex  confirm success criteria and agree to sample ticket dataset by EOD Friday.
2) Priya  confirm staging access and preferred SDK language.
3) Rishi / Dylan  please review the integration checklist and flag any concerns (especially on streaming and tool-calling).

Thanks  looking forward to getting started.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: ACME POC  streaming & tool-calling details (Python snippets)

Hi Alex / Priya  quick technical note from Dylan (Redwood eng):

Streaming semantics:
- We support server-sent events (SSE) and a chunked HTTP streaming mode in the SDKs. Partial tokens are emitted as they are generated; each chunk includes a token index and delta text. The client can commit partial outputs locally or wait for finalization.
- Backpressure: the SDKs expose a high-water mark; if the client cannot keep up the connection will buffer up to a configurable limit and then return a 429-like signal. For the POC we recommend the default buffer of 8MB and monitoring metrics for buffer pressure.

Tool-calling and delivery guarantees:
- Tool calls are delivered via webhook callback to the URL you register. We guarantee at-least-once delivery but add an idempotency-key header for each call. We recommend that ACME implement idempotency on your side (best practice) and design handlers to be idempotent.

- Retries: exponential backoff up to 5 attempts; we log attempts and provide a webhook delivery trace in the console.

Auth & SDK snippets (Python):
- Short-lived staging key: exchange via our console or use the SDK helper to request a token using a service account. Example (pseudocode):
  from redwood import RedwoodClient
  client = RedwoodClient(api_key="STAGING_KEY")
  # streaming call
  with client.stream_generate(model="rwd-base-1", prompt=prompt) as stream:
      for chunk in stream:
          print(chunk.text, end="")

Next steps from our side:
- I'll attach a minimal Python example to the shared Drive (redwood-sdk-integration-guide.md).
- We'll provide canary rollout guidance: start at 5% traffic on staging then 25% before full staging soak.

Let me know if you want a short Zoom breakout with Priya to walk through the snippet.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
